title: Almost-Linear-Time Maximum-Cardinality Matching in General Graphs
coverage:
Read in detail: Sections 1-5, 9 and 10, plus the main lemma and recursion proofs of Section 7 and the sampling lemma of Section 6. The rest of Sections 6-8 was only skimmed: the routing-helper overlay and router, and the backend update and forest-lifting machinery (Lemma update:flat-lift, class edits, recourse). I checked the following by hand.
(a) Exchange-projection identities: y' = y + F_src - F_snk, x' >= 0, the reachable set R being exactly captive, L h(R) < c w(R), and coarser-ledger debt payment of at least w(R) from Lemma match:deletion.
(b) Hall/submodularity tight-set alternative and both factor-critical exposure cases, including the captive-exposure Hall inequality.
(c) Soundness of the capacity-one cut witness and of the refinement min-cut.
(d) Walk-survival and hit-probability bounds w^T H <= L.
(e) Stall lemma: alternating-path prefixes entering bins at bases; r >= K/2 from g_* and the blocker bound; clipping and augmentation giving s'(Z) >= Lr - 2CN; the ratio exceeding 1/2.
(f) Local threshold test: optimistic domination, lock-preserving augmentation, the comparator ratio (A+ - A-)/(A+ + A-) > 1/2, integral rounding via the small-violation lemma, the expanded-weight bound 11(P+1), and local recovery of the full residual cut.
(g) Parent debt bound and the reset-cost sum.
(h) Priced-step constants (accept threshold 2qV, step scale mu, g^T h >= q^2/400) and LOW soundness against M^{-10/a}/4 > 2q.
(i) Bottom-level threshold Bellman-Ford range, and b^{-2d} = M^{-(4a-8)/a^2} >= M^{-10/a}.
(j) Matrix Bernstein constants in the sampling lemma.
(k) Benes-network cardinality reduction counting, path-gadget degree reduction (4e - v), and the f-factor reduction.
(l) Error union bounds and the dovetailing envelope construction.
main_claim: One uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm finds a maximum-cardinality matching in a simple n-vertex, m-edge graph in C p^{1+eta(p)} instructions on every path (p = n+m, eta -> 0), succeeding with probability at least 2/3. An f-factor corollary follows from a linearithmic reduction. The core is a fixed-parameter perfect-matching search on subcubic graphs in S^{1+O(1/a)+o_a(1)} time. It uses multiscale debt ledgers over bins (factor-critical odd blocks) and rows, a log-barrier top objective that is driven by priced min-ratio-cycle steps, and a dynamic flat-cycle backend.
sibling_notes: The family 120 board was empty when I checked. This paper is self-contained and does not depend on companion papers. The backend proof cites Chen et al.'s IncrementalGraphs (Lemma 2.7, Theorem 3.6, Section 4.5) and KMPG2023 for dynamic-tree and forest-copy constructions, but re-proves the interface it needs. Sections 6-8 deserve a dedicated deep pass if another branch has capacity: the routing helper's overlay and router, the frozen decomposition, and the lifting and recourse maintenance.
